properties.areaDesc: Yavapai, AZ
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 4:14PM MST until November 17 at 9:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 414 PM MST, a rise of 6 feet has occurred upstream of Page Springs
at Sedona, with further rises possible. Flash flooding is expected to
begin along Oak Creek in the Page Springs area within the next few
hours.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornville, Jordan, and Page Springs.

For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 4:00pm the stage was 1.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.

For Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 3:45pm the stage was 8.19 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Likely to cause minor flooding downstream in Page
Springs area near stream gage OACA3 4 to 6 hours later.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Verde River, Spring Creek, Oak Creek, Turkey Creek and Dry Creek.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 915 PM MST THIS EVENING FOR YAVAPAI COUNTY

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 6:09PM EST until November 17 at 7:15PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northern Broward County in southeastern Florida...
Southeastern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 715 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 609 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pompano Beach, Boca Raton, Deerfield Beach, Margate, Lighthouse
Point, Coconut Creek, Parkland, Hillsboro Beach, Boca Pointe,
Boca Del Mar, Mission Bay, North Pompano Beach, Hillsboro
Ranches, Pompano Beach Airport, Hillsboro Pines and Sandalfoot
Cove.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 4:00PM MST until November 17 at 6:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 400 PM MST, a river gauge on Oak Creek at Sedona continued to rise
rapidly, with a rise of over 6 feet in the last 2 hours. Water levels
remain elevated upstream of Sedona, likely leading to additional
rises on Oak Creek. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek.

For Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 3:45pm the stage was 8.19 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 5.0 feet: Multiple private low water crossings and bridges over
Oak Creek above Sedona become impassable.
At 7.0 feet: Likely to cause minor flooding downstream in Page
Springs area near stream gage OACA3 4 to 6 hours later.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sedona, Munds Park, Indian Gardens, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State
Park and Cathedral Rock.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Midgely Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing" and Crescent Moon
Ranch.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek and Dry Beaver Creek.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 17 at 1:45PM AKST until November 20 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a
light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass,
periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning,
with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches.

* WHERE...Mixed precipitation in Anchorage / Eagle River (all
elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, SW Kenai Peninsula, NW Kenai
Peninsula; heavy snowfall for Interior Kenai Peninsula, and
Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An atmospheric river is on track to move
across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the
thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that
overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However,
warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface
temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee
of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the
warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light
freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for
the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the
previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating
snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most
likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.
properties.instruction:

driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 1:32PM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on
snow is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This
includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam
Gulch.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday
morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches
of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with
elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday
afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch
per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack
may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying
and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways.
Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 4 inches
of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with
elevation. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an inch per hour
are possible between 3PM Wednesday through 3PM Thursday.
Southerly to southeasterly winds will shift to more easterly

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 2:27PM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.3 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso Bay and San
Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 5 AM WEDNESDAY TO 10 AM PST THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 17 at 2:27PM PST until November 18 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from
Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday
to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM
Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from
Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday
to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM
Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 17 at 12:34PM AKST until November 18 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 45 to 55 mph with gusts to 75 mph; winds turn
westerly beginning this evening.

* WHERE...Pribilof Islands.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A short lull of high winds will occur this
afternoon before a second peak in westerly winds occurs this
evening through Wednesday morning with winds gusting to 75 mph. As
a result of the long duration of westerly winds, wave heights of 25
to 30 ft within 15 to 20 nautical miles of Saint Paul are expected
through Wednesday afternoon.

Rain will mix with and change over to snow early Wednesday morning.
In conjunction with strong winds, visibility may drop to as low as
one-half mile at times in stronger snow showers Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.

properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Wednesday, for the
Mon Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in creeks and normally dry washes is

shortly in the advisory area.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Clear Creek, Toms Creek, West Webber Creek and Corduroy Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Payson, Pine, Strawberry, Mesa Del Caballo, East Verde Estates,

southbound between mile markers 250 and 251. State Route 87
between mile markers 250 and 273...and between mile markers 275
and 281.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Geronimo Boy Scout Camp, Houston Mesa Campground, Rumsey Park and
Green Valley Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Water Wheel Falls.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 12:54PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected in the Eastern Sierra. For elevations
between 5,000 and 8,000 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 10
to 18 inches expected. For elevations between 8,000 and 9,500 feet,
storm total snow accumulations of 18 to 36 inches expected. Locally
higher totals expected above 9,500 feet. Winds could gust as high
as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Sierra Slopes.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening
commutes. Strong winds could cause extensive damage to trees and
power lines. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will
likely become slick and hazardous. Whiteout conditions are expected
and will make travel treacherous and potentially life-threatening.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. Motorists should use
extreme caution if travel is absolutely necessary.

Puerto Rico, including beaches in Aguada and Rincon.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 1:44PM CST until November 19 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 AM CST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, until 6 AM CST
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1105 PM tonight and again at 1049 PM Thursday night.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 2:24PM EST until November 20 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM this evening to 10 AM EST Wednesday.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued due to
stagnant conditions and calm winds. Fine particulate levels are
expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active
children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as
asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure.

in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.

at 8:15 AM EST Tuesday was 17.1 feet.

stage at 17.1 to 17.2 feet.

in the week due to the additional heavy rainfall expected.

issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Tuesday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 16 at 3:18PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole,
Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie,
and Martin counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast
through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast
with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest
potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal
counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
